**Forward Bias Operation:**
When the positive terminal of a DC source is connected to the p-type and the negative terminal to the n-type of a PN junction diode, it is forward biased. The applied voltage opposes the built-in potential barrier, narrowing the depletion region and allowing a large forward current to flow easily once the threshold voltage ($0.3\text{ V}$ for Ge, $0.7\text{ V}$ for Si) is exceeded.

**Reverse Bias Operation:**
When the positive terminal is connected to the n-type and the negative terminal to the p-type, the diode is reverse biased. The applied voltage aids the barrier potential, widening the depletion region and preventing major carrier flow, resulting in only a minuscule reverse saturation current due to minority carriers.

**V-I Characteristic Curve:**
```
  I (mA)
    ^         Forward Bias
    |           /
    |         / 
    |       /   
    |     /     
    +-------------------> V (Volts)
    |          | 
    |          | Reverse Saturation Current
    |          V 
    v
             Reverse Bias (Breakdown)
```
proTip: Remember that in forward bias, the depletion layer decreases, while in reverse bias, it increases.
